messages:
Amanda (support): Hey folks — hitting intermittent failures when customers use JSON mode on /v1/generate. Two things to call out: 1) some responses come back as 401 HTML pages which then break our pydantic/zod schema parsing, 2) billing shows token usage for those failed attempts. Latency also spikes ~2-3s for the affected requests. Repro below. Raj (eng): Can you paste a minimal curl + payload and a request-id? Also, what model + json_schema are you using? Amanda (support): Minimal repro below. Using model: open-llm-v1 (quantized). json_schema: {"type":"object","properties":{"answer":{"type":"string"}},"required":["answer"]} curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer ' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'X-Request-ID: req-abc-123' -d '{"model":"open-llm-v1","json_mode":true,"prompt":"Q: add 1+1\nA:","max_tokens":50}' Response body (observed): ...

401 Unauthorized

Pydantic parse error we see in user logs: "ValidationError: 1 validation error for OutputModel answer field required (type=value_error.missing)" — but the real root cause is the HTML 401 page failing to be parsed as JSON. Eve (billing): If those requests are failing with 401 we shouldn't be billing tokens. Do you have timestamps and customer IDs? We need examples to credit retroactively. Amanda (support): Affected customer: BrightFin (cust-981). Timestamps: 2026-03-16T14:12:34Z, 2026-03-16T14:12:41Z. Request IDs: req-abc-123, req-abc-128. Billing shows 34 tokens billed each time. Oliver (sre): This smells like the auth proxy returning an HTML error page (maybe token expiry or a rate-limit block) instead of JSON. Our JSON-mode parser assumes content-type: application/json and attempts to decode body directly which then raises the schema error. We should short-circuit on non-JSON content-type or status != 200. Raj (eng): Agreed. Two quick mitigations: 1) change parser to verify Content-Type starts with application/json and fail fast with a structured error (so pydantic doesn't try to validate an empty object), 2) log raw body and request-id for debugging. I'll prototype a fix on the runtime layer. Amanda (support): Also note latency spikes — customers report ~2-3s extra. Example trace attached: route /v1/generate -> auth-proxy (timeout retry) -> runtime. Might be our auth proxy trying a stale KMS call. inc-bot: Ticket #INC-1234 created for BrightFin. Severity: P2. Owner: Raj (eng). Eve (billing): I'll start a credit for cust-981 for the two timestamps once we have the full request_ids and token counts. Please add invoice ids if available. Amanda (support): Invoice for BrightFin: INV-2026-03-09-981 — I will attach the full list in the ticket. Oliver (sre): For repro, try disabling token refresh on the client and run a small script to hit /v1/generate with an invalid token header — verify we return JSON error with proper status and body. If we return HTML, it's proxy-level. Amanda (support): Repro steps I asked customer to run and they confirmed: 1) curl with expired token -> see HTML 401 body 2) same curl with valid token -> valid JSON schema response 3) they saw billing entries for both attempts Raj (eng): I'll open a PR to make JSON-mode parser check Content-Type and respond with a clear 499-like error (structured) when upstream returns non-json. Also will add a small sanitizer that strips leading whitespace and non-json chars so we don't try to feed HTML into pydantic. Will include correlation id logging. ETA: today EOD. Amanda (support): Thanks. Please also include a unit test that covers HTML error body -> parser fails with parseable error, and an integration test for the auth-proxy returning 401 HTML. Raj (eng): Will do. I'll ping here when PR is up. @Eve once we have the request ids + token counts we'll coordinate refunds. Eve (billing): 👍 once you tag the request ids I'll process a manual credit for cust-981 and open a billing check to ensure auth-failed requests are excluded from token counts going forward. Amanda (support): Great, escalating to BrightFin account contact with the incident ticket and expected timeline. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
